questions: When reversing edges, does the reversal apply to all edges in the graph globally, or only to edges incident to the current vertex?
Can the edge reversal operation be performed multiple times, and if so, does each reversal toggle direction (so two reversals restore original orientation)?
Is the cost X incurred each time we reverse edges, regardless of whether the reversal changes reachable edges from the current vertex?
Are self-loops (u_i = v_i) allowed, and if so, how do they behave under reversal?
When moving along a directed edge, can we choose any outgoing edge, including ones that may have been created by a previous reversal?
Is the goal to reach vertex N exactly, or can we pass through it and continue moving?
If multiple edges exist between the same pair of vertices in the same direction, are they considered distinct for movement?
Does the reversal operation have any effect if performed when no edges exist (e.g., at an isolated vertex)?
